stated: The Conservative Party will cut anti-social behaviour in town centres by rolling out Hotspot Policing to all forces, expanding community payback, and legislating to evict social tenants who repeatedly disrupt neighbours.

source.quote: Cut anti-social behaviour in town centres by rolling out Hotspot Policing, expanding community payback and legislating to evict social tenants who repeatedly disrupt their neighbours.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets anti-social behaviour through policing, payback schemes, and eviction powers — a core crime/safety measure with real potential effect on ASB rates and public safety.
Legislating to evict social tenants for repeated ASB directly affects security of tenure for social housing occupants — a concrete O1 indicator.

Hotspot policing concentrates surveillance and enforcement power in specific areas; eviction legislation imposes a serious state-coercive sanction (loss of home) on social tenants for behavioural infringements — both bear concretely on freedom from state coercion and privacy indicators.

ASB is a documented driver of community fragmentation and reduced social trust; a genuine reduction in town-centre ASB would plausibly move social-trust and belonging indicators in affected areas, earning a real (if downstream) verdict on O15.

membership_note: Three-component policy: the safety effect lands on O5 (its stated purpose), the coercive enforcement mechanisms earn a separate O10 worsening verdict, and the community-cohesion channel is concrete enough (ASB→trust→belonging) to warrant O15. No material fiscal commitment is specified so O12 is not triggered; no discrimination/voting angle for O9.
